summary.headline: SBI Q2 FY27 net profit ₹23,038 crore; treasury MTM loss ~₹1,277 crore weighed on operating profit, which grew 7.28% YoY to ₹34,226 crore.
summary.overview: SBI reported Q2 FY27 net profit of ₹23,038 crore and domestic NIM of 3.11%, with H1 ROA at 1.14% and ROE at 18.68%. Operating profit rose 7.28% YoY to ₹34,226 crore, but management attributed the muted growth to a treasury MTM loss of about ₹1,275-1,277 crore and upfronted overheads of about ₹850 crore. Deposits grew 12.27% YoY and gross NPA fell to 1.39%, its lowest in over two decades. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 14-15% credit growth, ROA around 1%, NIM not below 3%, and ROE of 15% through the cycle. The call focused heavily on accounting classification of the NSE and SBI Mutual Fund stake sales and on the ECL transition impact of ₹19,500 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Improved QoQ; management cited ~11 bps expansion
Lowest in more than two decades

financial_highlights.value: ₹6,000 crore in Q2 FY27 vs ₹7,470 crore a year earlier
₹15,531 crore (staff ₹17,452 crore? per DMD, overheads ₹16,531 crore)
financial_highlights.change: Overheads +15% YoY; ~9% YoY ex ₹850 crore upfronted
H1 (March to September) corporate book up ~1%

financial_highlights.metric: ROA excluding SBI Funds Management stake sale gain

segments.name: Retail / Home loans
segments.commentary: Home and home-related portfolio crossed ₹10 lakh crore; management said home loan growth is trailing industry and attributed slowdown to developers' inventory build-up and weaker Bengaluru purchases. Personal loans grew 7.48%.

segments.name: Auto loans
segments.commentary: Pricing was tweaked as a hook product; management said October showed robust growth and the bank is back in the segment.

segments.name: Agriculture / Agri gold loan
segments.commentary: Agri gold loan LTV around 60-61%. Three drought-declared states have potential restructuring portfolio of about ₹10,000 crore, subject to farmer consent; past uptake has been low.

segments.name: SME / ECLGS
segments.commentary: ECLGS 5.0 is fully utilised at ₹2.5 lakh crore system-wide; SBI's ECLGS accounts total about ₹28,800 crore, around 50% of SME growth, priced at 9%.

segments.name: Treasury / Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: SBI Funds Management listed in the quarter; the 6.35% stake sale gain was ₹7,288 crore booked through P&L. NSE stake sale gains went to AFS reserve (about ₹2,500 crore); remaining NSE holding MTM about ₹11,000 crore.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth guidance of 14-15% for FY27 reiterated; management expects H2 to be busy and says the guidance is easily achievable with ~₹7-7.8 lakh crore corporate pipeline.
NIM guidance of not less than 3% maintained; management sees tailwinds from 25 bps EBLR and 15 bps MCLR repricing and possible 50 bps repo hike in December, and said NIM could be above 3%.
ROA around 1%, ROE of 15%, and NIM above 3% maintained through the cycle, with ECL impact said to be factored in.
Overheads growth target not beyond 10% YoY; further upfronting of expenses planned in Q3 to smooth the Q4 cost bump.

ECL transition impact about ₹19,500 crore (net of tax and existing provisions) on loans; regulatory dispensation allows spread over four years from 1 April 2027; P&L impact to be measured from 30 June 2027 and guidance on earnings deferred for a couple of quarters.
Management expects G-Sec yields to fall below 7% by end of FY27; house view calls for a 50 bps repo hike in December.
capex_capacity: Excess SLR of about ₹3.5-3.7 lakh crore currently, versus ₹4.8 lakh crore as of September, providing liquidity without competing for deposits.
FCNR(B) mobilisation of $10.9 billion against a $10 billion target; $8.83 billion leveraged through foreign offices, with foreign office NIM down only 2 bps.
Seva Sarathi deployed at over 9,500 high-footfall branches; Re-KYC digital updates above 1.2 crore since June, cutting branch intervention by more than 50%.
YONO registrations above 11 crore; YONO Bharat device-neutral platform in development. SBI CyRIS cyber centre inaugurated.
No plans to list further subsidiaries in the next couple of years, per management; YES Bank stake not being exited at present.
demand_pricing: Deposits +12.27% YoY; CASA franchise described as stable base. Management said the NIM expansion came from lower deposit costs (FCNR(B) used to reduce wholesale deposits, higher daily average balances in savings and current accounts) and higher advance yields.
Corporate book flat in H1 (about 1%) per analyst; management said YTD growth is seasonally slow and Q2 corporate growth was 16%.
Management deliberately let go of low-yield working capital, T-bill linked and refinance deals; corporate working capital utilisation fell.
Loan mix: MCLR 27%, EBLR 32%, T-bill linked 17%, fixed rate 21% of domestic advances.
NII grew 4.65% QoQ vs average domestic earning assets growth of 1.03%.
Operating income growth 8.44% vs operating expense growth 9%, per management answer.

qa_highlights.question: How will credit growth reach the 14-15% target given weak H1, and where will it come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 was strong by industry standards, H2 is seasonally busier, and the ~₹7 lakh crore corporate pipeline supports the 14-15% guidance; growth will come from corporate, gold, home and auto loans.

qa_highlights.question: How were treasury and NSE/SBI Mutual Fund gains classified, and where did the ₹6,011 crore treasury profit go?
qa_highlights.answer: NSE is classified as AFS, so gains go to the AFS reserve and not P&L; SBI Mutual Fund sale gains went through P&L. Treasury was a net loss of about ₹1,275-1,277 crore MTM due to bond yield moves, combined with the AMC gain in other income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating expenses and overheads rise, and how much was upfronted?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹850 crore of overheads was upfronted (₹450 crore map services, ₹250 crore IT, ₹150 crore vendors). Ex this, YoY overhead growth is about 9%; PSLC purchases earlier in the year also added to business acquisition costs (₹118 crore in Q1 and ₹583 crore in Q2).

qa_highlights.question: Where will NIM land given it is above the 3% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the 3% floor, citing EBLR and MCLR repricing tailwinds, possible December repo hike and excess SLR; it declined to give a higher number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition impact and will standard asset provisioning rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Net ECL impact of about ₹19,500 crore on loans after tax and existing provisions, excluding HTM fair valuation and crop loans, which are still under discussion; P&L effect to be assessed from 30 June 2027 and no guidance on earnings yet.

qa_highlights.question: How much agri restructuring is likely?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹10,000 crore potential restructuring across three drought-declared states, subject to farmer consent; historically only a few avail it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is home loan growth lagging and is there a consumer demand issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it partly to developer supply and inventory build-up, with some purchase slowdown in Bengaluru; the bank is gaining share but will not outpace the industry.

risks_watch: ECL implementation from 1 April 2027 (₹19,500 crore transition impact; standard asset provisioning could add volatility); outcome to be visible from the 30 June 2027 measurement.
Treasury volatility from bond yields; Q2 included ~₹1,277 crore MTM loss and Q3 expense upfronting may further smooth costs.
Deposit cost pressure if system liquidity tightens or deposit rates must rise; FCNR(B) leverage of $8.83 billion from foreign offices.
YES Bank stake and related litigation (sub judice); management declined to comment on the legal process and said there are no plans to exit.
Agri stress from drought-hit states (about ₹10,000 crore restructuring potential) and ECLGS 5.0 utilisation at ₹2.5 lakh crore system-wide.
summary.management_tone: Confident on core metrics, NIM, credit growth and asset quality, while openly defensive on the reported profit and operating profit optics, which management attributed to treasury losses and upfronted overheads. Evasive on YES Bank legal matters (sub judice) and on ECL P&L impact, and declined to change the accounting presentation.
key_quotes: And why you don't see that ₹6,000 crore post-tax here , is essentially because of the Treasury losses.
NSE, we have classified under Available For Sale category. If it is AFS, the divestment will go to AFS reserve. It is not routed through the P&L.
So, we have set out a $10 billion target, I think we have exceeded the target, 10. 9 was the final number, and we are fine with that.
But I can tell you that it not less than 3% is an important guidance which I am giving to you.
So, I stick to my guidance, an annual guidance of return on assets of 1%, net interest margin not less than 3% and ROE of 15% , through the cycles you are assured of.
We will not compromise on the asset quality to earn more.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 credit growth of 14-15% and says it is achievable with a ₹7-7.8 lakh crore corporate pipeline and 16% corporate growth guided for the rest of H2, but H1 corporate book was only about 1% up, so backing is partial; no new capacity was disclosed and utilisation was not stated.
